title_en: Write the series style once, reuse everywhere
content_en:
1. Style choice: to test a specific style, write it down as the style text and it is used; also tell the text model that writes the image prompts about the style so it adapts the prompts it generates accordingly. To let the text model choose the best style for the project, leave the style empty and ask it to define a style fitting the project.
2. Style wrapper: each image prompt carries the line Follow this style: with the style text in quotes.
3. First chat turn: tell the image model what images it is going to generate and for what, then give The style we want you to follow is: with the style text, and Also follow those rules: with the system instructions.
4. Prompt assembly: the prompt passed to the image model contains not only the generated description of the characters but also the style and the system instructions.

title_en: Style prompts: one line or long caption
content_en: A prompt that carries a style can be a one-line instruction of one or two sentences, or a long description of 220-260 words written as a caption of an already existing photo. The long form covers style, camera angle, colors by plane, light, foreground and background, and the overall impression.
applies_when_en: The prompt writer decides whether to write the style briefly (a label or a fragment) or as an extended description of a finished shot.
caveats_en: Descriptive prompts for this model share a structure: one or two sentences with subject, attributes and action, followed by a comma-separated tail of style and technique descriptors that ends with an explicit plain background. (models: lite)
Most sample prompts are one to three sentences: output type or medium + subject + setting. (models: lite)
NotebookLM prompts are short and often written as fragments; they combine a content or task instruction with brief style descriptors rather than describing individual slides. (models: pro)

Imagen 3 Customization person examples use comma-separated descriptor lists including quality tags ('high quality, 4k, masterpiece, super details'), while the product example uses full descriptive sentences; Imagen models are retired. (models: other)
